Graphs of Distribution of Current Law Tax Burden and Income by
Source
Annually, the Office of Tax Analysis releases baseline distribution tables of Federal Taxes (Table
001) and Cash Income by Source (Table 002). These tables report estimates of income and taxes
for the first year of the ten-year budget period under current law and the Administration’s
economic forecast. Figures 1 and 2 below summarize the 2024 baseline estimates.1
AVERAGE FEDERAL TAX RATES BY ADJUSTED FAMILY CASH INCOME, 2024
FIGURE 1
Figure 1 shows average tax rates for the individual income tax, payroll tax, corporate income
tax, and excise taxes separately and in total.2 All refundable credits (including the advanced
portion of the Premium Tax Credit) are included as negative taxes in U.S. Treasury distribution
tables. As a result, individual income taxes are shown as negative, on average, for low-income
1 The tables corresponding to these figures for 2024 are available here. For a summary explanation of the U.S. Treasury’s
distributional analysis methodology look here. For a detailed explanation of Treasury’s distributional analysis methodology, see
OTA Technical Paper 8.
2 Figure 1 corresponds to Distribution Table 2024 001, Distribution of Families, Cash Income, and Federal Taxes under 2024
Current Law.
U.S. Department of the Treasury
Office of Tax Analysis
November, 2023

on average, in payroll tax than any other Federal tax. Average corporate income and average
excise taxes (including customs duties) are very low compared to average individual income and
average payroll taxes for almost all families.
DISTRIBUTION OF INCOME SHARES BY INCOME SOURCE, 2024
FIGURE 2
Figure 2 shows the distribution of cash income.3 The height of each bar is the share of total cash
income received by each income decile. The sources of total income for each decile are shown
by colored sections: transfer income (dark blue), labor income (red) and capital income (light
blue). Detail for the top decile is shown on the right side of the figure (the sum of the 3 bars on
the right equal the bar for the top 10 percent and the sum of labor income, transfer income and
capital income on the right sum to the source shares for the top 10 percent).
As shown in the figure, families in the top decile of the income distribution receive 45 percent
of total income and families in the top 1 percent receive 19 percent of total income. Families in

DOC_D5DC1F_E005.text:
3
the next highest income decile (80 to 90th percentile) receive 15 percent of total income.
Families in the bottom 10 percent of the income distribution receive less than 1 percent of total
income.
Labor income is the largest source of income for each decile (the red share of each bar is larger
than the dark blue or light blue). As a share of total income, labor income is over 75 percent of
total income for families in the sixth decile (50-60th percentile) thru the ninth decile (80 to 90th
percentile) of the income distribution.
Only families in the top decile have a significant share of their income from capital (light blue
section of each bar). For families in the bottom half of the distribution, income from capital is
less than 5 percent of total income.
Transfer income is only a significant share of total income for the lower income deciles. Notably
total transfer income is higher for middle-income families than the lowest income families (the
dark blue sections of each bar are tallest for middle-income families) because not all sources of
transfer income are means tested (e.g. social security benefits).
U.S. Department of the Treasury
Office of Tax Analysis
November, 2023

Efficacy, Patient Stratification & Primary Endpoint Audit
Date: August 15, 2026
Doc ID: MED-2026-CT3
Multimodal Document Intelligence | Verified Formal Report
1. Executive Summary & Study Design Overview
A multicenter, double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled Phase III study evaluated the therapeutic
efficacy and safety profile of NeuroShield (VX-409) across 1,200 participants across 18 medical centers.
The primary cognitive retention endpoint was met with high statistical significance (p < 0.001).
At Week 48, 88.4% of subjects in the High-Dose (100mg) cohort demonstrated cognitive stability versus
51.2% in the placebo cohort, demonstrating substantial clinical neuroprotection.

Biomarker Modulation & Pharmacovigilance Safety
Secondary Endpoints, Plaque Clearance & Biostatistical Proof
Date: August 15, 2026
Doc ID: MED-2026-CT3
Multimodal Document Intelligence | Verified Formal Report
2. Biomarker Efficacy & Adverse Event Profile
Positron emission tomography (PET) imaging demonstrated a mean 42.8% reduction in cortical amyloid
plaque burden in the 100mg cohort compared to a 4.2% increase in the placebo group. Serious Adverse Events
(SAEs) occurred in 4.2% of active drug subjects versus 3.8% of placebo subjects (p = 0.72, non-significant),
confirming that VX-409 exhibits an excellent clinical safety and tolerability window.

3. Biostatistical Formulation & Hazard Ratio Verification
Biostatistical Formulations:
  - Hazard Ratio (HR) = 0.58 (95% CI: [0.47, 0.71], p < 0.0001 via Cox Proportional Hazards Model)
  - Cognitive Decline Event Rates: Placebo = 48.8%, High-Dose VX-409 = 11.6%
  - Absolute Risk Reduction (ARR) = EventRate_Placebo - EventRate_Active
      ARR = 48.8% - 11.6% = 37.2% (0.372)
  - Number Needed to Treat (NNT) = 1 / ARR
      NNT = 1 / 0.372 = 2.69 patients (Treating ~3 patients prevents 1 cognitive decline event)
  - Relative Risk Reduction (RRR) = (ARR / EventRate_Placebo) * 100% = (37.2% / 48.8%) * 100% = 76.23%.
